pc_onoff Remote Power Control Architecture & Decision Guide

Long image

A

Answer

Two LAN gateways—Home Phone or Home Assistant—bridge WAN and Google Home voice into local UDP packets that control your PC. (繁體中文版)1

  1. Target PCs only listen on LAN UDP 9 and UDP 9877; they never need a public IPv6 address.2
  2. Private LAN and Tailscale sources run bare commands with zero secrets, while public IPs fail closed without HMAC-SHA256.3
  3. Home Assistant holds switch intent for 25 seconds so Google Home does not bounce back to OFF during PC BIOS boot.4
  4. All four subsystems isolate parsing, trust, and OS power logic inside deep modules with zero external runtime packages.5

Applies to4 subsystemsUDP 9 & 9877TCP 9876Home Assistant 2024.1

1

How do the two LAN gateways reach the target PC?

Diagram structure
  • Remote Phone remote_phone
  • Google Home google_home
  • Home Phone home_phone
  • Home Assistant ha_gateway
  • PC NIC UDP 9 pc_nic
  • PC Daemon 9877 pc_daemon
  • remote_phone → home_phone · TCP 9876
  • google_home → ha_gateway · Voice switch
  • home_phone → pc_nic · WoL packet
  • home_phone → pc_daemon · Power UDP
  • ha_gateway → pc_nic · WoL packet
  • ha_gateway → pc_daemon · Power UDP
  • remote_phone → pc_daemon · Direct LAN

The target PC stays inside your home network; the gateway handles public IPv6, MQTT, or Google Home voice ingress.6

  1. Google Home ↗

    Routes "turn on/off PC" voice commands to Home Assistant.

  2. Home Assistant ↗

    Emits UDP 9 Wake-on-LAN or UDP 9877 power datagrams on LAN.

  3. Home Phone ↗

    Listens on TCP 9876 and MQTT, then forwards to local UDP.

  4. PC Daemon 9877 ↗

    Checks CIDR trust and HMAC signature before calling OS power APIs.

2

Why does the Google Home switch stay ON while the PC boots?

Diagram structure
  • Google Home user
  • PcPowerSwitch switch
  • Coordinator coord
  • Target PC pc
  • user → switch · Turn on PC
  • switch → coord · async_wake()
  • coord → pc · UDP 9 Magic Packet (102 B)
  • coord → switch · Report ON (hold 25s)
  • coord → pc · Poll Ping at t=5s (BIOS boot)
  • pc → coord · No reply (keep ON)
  • coord → pc · Reconcile Ping at +26s
  • pc → coord · Reply OK (converged ON)

A PC takes 15 to 35 seconds after Wake-on-LAN to answer ping; a 25-second hold blocks premature offline polls.4

  1. PcPowerSwitch ↗

    Calls async_wake to send the UDP 9 magic packet and flip ON.

  2. Coordinator ↗

    Holds intent ON for 25s so early failed probes cannot flip OFF.

  3. Target PC ↗

    Converges early when reachable, or reconciles at +26s.

Why do lock and reboot leave the switch ON?

Both lock and reboot keep the machine powered. PcOnOffCoordinator only flips the switch OFF and starts the 25-second hold window for shutdown, sleep, and hibernate.

3

How do trusted LAN and public HMAC-SHA256 traffic split?

Source IP classification decides trust automatically: local LAN and Tailscale need no secret, while public IPs fail closed.3

Diagram structure
  • Incoming packet packet_in
  • LAN or Tailscale? trusted_q
  • Parse ts & nonce check_env
  • Valid HMAC & window? sig_ok_q
  • Drop & log error reject_cmd
  • Execute OS power dispatch_os
  • check_env → sig_ok_q · ±300s
  • packet_in → trusted_q
  • sig_ok_q → dispatch_os · yes
  • sig_ok_q → reject_cmd · no
  • trusted_q → check_env · no
  • trusted_q → dispatch_os · yes
PropertyTrusted LAN & TailscalePublic IPv4 & IPv6
Covered CIDRs127/8, RFC1918, 169.254/16, 100.64/10, ::1, fe80::/10, fc00::/7All non-trusted public unicast addresses
Shared secretZero-config LANNone neededFails closedRequired (pc_secret or helper_secret)
Wire formatBare action (e.g. shutdown)<cmd>|ts=<unix>|nonce=<16hex>|sig=<64hex>
Replay defenseRelies on local LAN or Tailscale WireGuardTriple guard±300s clock window + 600s nonce cache + daemon boot cutoff

How are the four subsystems split into deep modules?

Each subsystem hides protocol and OS complexity inside one deep module while transport and UI layers stay thin.5

Diagram structure
  • wake-on-lan-for-android root
  • computer (Rust Daemon) comp
  • dispatch.rs + power.rs comp_disp
  • auth.rs + crypto.rs + net.rs comp_auth
  • wakeonlanhomephone (Home Phone) home
  • PcActionDispatcher.kt + CommandAuth.kt home_disp
  • wakeonwanremotephone (Remote Phone) remote
  • RemoteNetworkUtil.kt + CommandAuth.kt remote_net
  • custom_components/pc_onoff (HA) ha
  • Layer 1: protocol + probe + state ha_l1
  • Layer 2-3: coordinator + switch + button ha_l2
  • root → comp
  • comp → comp_disp
  • comp → comp_auth
  • root → home
  • home → home_disp
  • root → remote
  • remote → remote_net
  • root → ha
  • ha → ha_l1
  • ha → ha_l2
